text:
emma: FYI vendor INV-2026-0453 (Porto Tech Soluções) billed VAT on the invoice but they marked the supply as B2B. They sent back 'micro-empresa' registration details — I think reverse-charge might apply. Holding payment until we confirm. Can tax confirm what evidence we need?

raj: @sophie can you confirm checklist? If reverse-charge applies we should credit and reissue with 0% VAT or ask vendor for corrected invoice. Also need to confirm whether OSS / special schemes are in play.

sophie: Quick notes — reverse charge for services inside EU applies when buyer is VAT-registered in another EU state and vendor supplies B2B. For PT vendors we need: 1) valid VAT number (VIES check screenshot), 2) vendor invoice explicitly stating "reverse charge" or equivalent, 3) proof buyer VAT (our EU VAT ID on PO/invoice). If vendor is under special small-business regime (isento/mono-scheme) they might still charge VAT.

sophie: Please attach vendor's VAT number + the email they sent. If they claim micro-empresa, get a statement from them that they're on the simplified regime and why they charged VAT. If no evidence, we should not pay VAT portion and ask for corrected invoice.

taxbot: Invoice parsed: INV-2026-0453 | vendor: Porto Tech Soluções | amount: EUR 12,500.00 | VAT: EUR 2,875.00 | currency: EUR | received_ts: 2312345600

emma: Pasting vendor reply below (redacted):

"Marta (Porto Tech): Our NIF is PT999888777 and we are registered as micro-empresa under CAE 6201. We charged VAT because we are not using the OSS and consider the sale domestic. We can reissue if you require reverse charge. Attached PDF: invoice_INV-2026-0453.pdf"

raj: OK — @sophie can you run a quick VIES check on PT999888777 and confirm whether it's valid and active? If VIES ok and our VAT ID is listed on PO, vendor should be allowed to zero-rate the invoice and note reverse charge. If they're refusing because of micro-empresa rules we may need a credit note + new invoice.

sophie: Did VIES check — PT999888777 returned "Valid" in VIES (screenshot uploaded to thread). However micro-empresa registration means they might not frequently use reverse charge. We need their explicit statement to treat it as B2B sale and a corrected invoice that references Article and reverse charge wording ("IVA - autoliquidação" or English "reverse charge").

sophie: Suggested email to vendor (copy this):
```
Hi Marta,

Thanks for the invoice. To process without VAT we need:
1) Reissued invoice with PT VAT number PT999888777 and our EU VAT ID (EU123456789).
2) Clear statement on the invoice that VAT is not charged under reverse charge (e.g., "IVA - autoliquidação / reverse charge").
3) A short written confirmation that the supply is B2B and that the vendor consents to treat this sale as such.

Once we have that we will process the invoice net of VAT.

Best,
Sophie (Redwood Tax)
```

emma: Sent that template to Marta at 09:14. She replied: "We can reissue, will do today." :thumbsup:

raj: Thanks. Finance: put payment hold on INV-2026-0453 for VAT portion only. If they reissue with reverse charge we'll pay net amount immediately and close. If they reissue incorrectly, escalate to legal/tax for final decision.

sophie: One additional flag — vendor also sent a US tax contact asking for W-9 because parent company in US wants to reconcile. Reminder: W-9 is only for US persons. For Portuguese legal entity we need local docs, not a W-9. If they send a W-9 claiming US entity, ask for proof of US tax residency and whether the invoicing entity is the same legal entity as on the invoice.

emma: Noted. I replied to vendor to confirm invoicing entity. Leaving payment on hold until we receive reissued invoice with reverse-charge line or an explicit refusal + reason.

raj: tagging @sophie for final sign-off once reissued invoice is uploaded. :white_check_mark:

sophie: I'll sign off after I see the corrected invoice and vendor confirmation. If they refuse, we'll request a credit note and then decide whether to gross-up or dispute the VAT with them.

emma: Closing loop — will report back when invoice reissued or vendor provides more detail.
